turns.text: Hi Ayan, good to start the week with you. What stood out today?

So today I mostly went through last week's search logs for the help centre. Honestly it was a bit of a surprise, about 12% of searches come back with nothing at all. A lot of them are just typos, like people typing refnd instead of refund.
That's a useful thing to find. What did the team decide to do about it?
I suggested we handle spelling mistakes first, since that's the biggest chunk, and the team agreed. The other stuff, like people using different words for the same thing, can wait.
Makes sense to start with the biggest piece. What's the one thing for tomorrow?
Tomorrow I'll try adding typo tolerance to search and see if refnd finds the refund article.

turns.text: Welcome back. Last time you were going to try typo tolerance in search. How did it go?

Good, I got it working on my machine. Now refnd finds the refund article, and bagage finds the baggage one. One thing I learned is you have to switch it off for really short words, otherwise visa starts matching vista and the results get weird.
That's a nice catch. What else happened today?
A new junior joined our team, so I spent most of the afternoon with them. I walked them through how the search and the nightly import fit together, and gave them a small first ticket to start with.
How did they take to it?
Pretty well I think. They asked good questions, and they already have a pull request open for the ticket.

Yes, it got merged this morning, they were really happy about that.
Nice. How was the rest of your day?

Honestly frustrating. The nightly article import now takes about 3 hours, so it runs into the morning and new help articles show up late in search. I couldn't figure out why yet, I spent the whole day just reading logs.
That sounds draining. Was there anything that went okay?
Yeah, I started a list of real traveller questions with the ML team so we can test the trip assistant properly. We have about 120 so far.

turns.text: Hi Ayan. How did today go?

Rough morning. Support pinged us that the trip assistant was telling travellers the old refund rules. Turns out the import was quietly skipping articles that had been edited, it only picked up new ones.
That sounds stressful. What did you do?
I found the bug, fixed it so it checks when an article was last edited, and re-ran the import for the articles it missed. The right answers were back in about 2 hours.
Good recovery. What's next on it?
Tomorrow I want to write up what happened and add an alert so this can't happen quietly again.

turns.text: Go ahead, tell me everything from today. I'll sort it out.

Okay. So I wrote up yesterday's incident, what broke, how we found it and what we changed, and I added an alert that fires if the import skips any edited articles. My lead said the write-up was really clear and shared it with the other teams, which felt nice.
Got it. Anything else?
Yes, I also found why the import is so slow. It handles articles one at a time, around 9,000 of them. Next week I want to make it work on several at once.
Thanks, that's a good way to end the week.

turns.text: Welcome back, Ayan. Last time I asked how many searches still come back empty after the typo fix. Do you have that now?
Yes! The typo fix went live today. Searches that come back empty went from about 12% to 7%, so that's a lot more people finding their article.
That's a real improvement. What else happened today?
I did a code review with the junior. Instead of just fixing things myself I asked questions, so they found most of the issues on their own. It took longer but I think it sticks better.
What's the plan for tomorrow?
Tomorrow I'll roll out the change that makes the import work on several articles at once.

turns.text: Hi Ayan. Last time I asked whether support tickets about missing articles went down after the typo fix. Any news?
A little, support said there are fewer 'I can't find it' tickets, but it's early to put a number on it.
Fair enough. How did the import rollout go?
Really well actually. I changed the nightly import to work on several articles at once, and it's about 50% faster now, so new articles are in search before people start work.
That's a big win. Was anything tricky about it?
Yeah, I learned the hard way that if I send too many at once, the article feed starts refusing requests. So I kept it to 5 at a time.

turns.text: Hi Ayan. What stood out today?

We finally ran the trip assistant through the test list with the ML team, it's 200 real traveller questions now. It got about 30 of them wrong, mostly baggage and visa questions. I went through each one and sent the ML team a list of what to fix in the prompts.
That's careful work. What else did you get done?
I built a small demo page so the product team can try the assistant themselves. It shows which help article each answer came from, so they can check it.
Nice. Anything else from today?
I also helped a teammate set up a dashboard for search traffic, mostly just pairing with them on it.

Anything you want to remember for next week?
